lanes.budget_rule_judgement: Question: does nodes = max(caller nodes, records + instances) override a caller's explicit safety bound, and is memory still bounded by a documented hard cap? Answer: (a) YES it overrides a smaller caller Budget::nodes for the record validation (proposal.rs:1740): a host that sets nodes = 500 no longer gets a refusal from that validation for an effect-heavy file (it may still be refused earlier by inspect_bytes of the document with its own nodes, :1724, when layers + operations exceed 500). (b) Budget::nodes was never the memory bound for the records: Builder holds every record and mapped stack before validation (proposal.rs:456, :1731), so the caller's nodes only turned an already-built proposal into an import failure. (c) Memory and validation work stay bounded: records <= Limits::max_layers (document.rs:349-350; default 8192, caller-owned) and kept instances <= MAX_EFFECTS_PER_PLAN 4096 (proposal.rs:530-534), so needed <= max_layers + 4096; this is TIGHTER than f6e5a49 for instances (then up to 1024 per layer x max_layers, no document cap). (d) The cap is documented only in the internal comment (proposal.rs:1733-1738) and the lane notes; the public surface does not say it: ProposalConfig.budget has no doc (proposal.rs:121) and DESCRIPTOR effect_limits says 'record_validation_nodes_are_sized_from_the_input_as_records_plus_instances' without 'a smaller caller nodes is raised' or the bound. Judgement: acceptable bound, public contract undocumented (PLAUSIBLE finding below).

findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-interop-psd/src/proposal.rs:530-534 (aggregate over every mapped stack, whole import Err(PsdError::EffectLimit)) and src/effects.rs:223, :357 (disabled instances and a disabled stack are mapped and counted) vs @f6e5a49 crates/hsk-studio-interop-psd/src/proposal.rs:1718 (only caller Budget::nodes) and crates/hsk-studio-composite/src/lower_extensions.rs:569-585 (pigment/composite count live instances of enabled stacks), crates/hsk-studio-composite/src/lower_render_plan.rs:430-434 (plan-wide limit is root-dependent and deliberately NOT applied document-wide)
findings.evidence: MAX_EFFECTS_PER_PLAN is a render-plan rule (effects of the layers one plan renders from a root, live instances only); composite's 07f6abd explicitly declines a document-wide count because it 'would over-refuse'. a5eff01 applies the same constant to the whole document, counting hidden layers, disabled instances and disabled stacks, and fails the WHOLE import. Consequences: (1) a valid PSD with more than 4096 mapped instances (e.g. 1400 layers x 3 effects, any of them hidden or switched off) cannot be imported at all, although every root composite would lower could be within the limit (and an over-limit root is already refused typed at lowering by 07f6abd); (2) regression: at f6e5a49 such a document imported under a caller Budget::nodes >= records + instances (no document cap; per-layer cap 1024); at 4d80e50 it fails regardless of the caller's budget. Neither consequence is disclosed: lane notes.not_fixed lists only the per-layer enabled-vs-mapped difference, and the commit subject says 'an effects-heavy valid PSD no longer fails the whole import'. A typed degrade with the same memory bound was available on the existing path: once the aggregate would pass 4096, map further stacks to the effects_over_budget typed loss (lfx2 stays byte-exact) and keep importing. Frequency of >4096-instance Photoshop documents UNVERIFIED (no corpus).
findings.remediation: Replace the whole-import Err at proposal.rs:530-534 by a per-stack typed loss once the running total would exceed MAX_EFFECTS_PER_PLAN (keeps records <= 4096 instances and the node bound), add a test with > 4096 instances that imports with typed losses; or the lead records an explicit decision accepting a document-wide cap that counts hidden/disabled instances and the lane discloses the f6e5a49 regression
